correctness.rationale: The correct ordinary three-cut facets are complements V minus T for disconnected triples T, not independent triples (total cut). Its Alexander dual K consists of subsets whose every three vertices induce a connected triple. Independent exhaustive enumeration through all 2^13 masks finds K f-vector (13,78,143,78), no size-five face. Independently assembled signed integral boundary operators have Smith factors all 1 with ranks ∂1=12, ∂2=66, ∂3=76, and consecutive boundary products zero. A star spanning tree in the complete 1-skeleton leaves 66 edge-path generators; 33 are trivial by triangles through vertex0 and the other 33 by triangular relators with precisely one remaining edge; hence π1(K)=1. Thus H2(K)=Z, H3(K)=Z², with no torsion or other reduced groups. Since K is simply connected and 3-dimensional, attaching 3-cells to a wedge of 2-spheres and integral unit Smith cancellations yields S²∨S³∨S³. Combinatorial Alexander duality on 13 vertices gives H_i(Δ3)≅H^{10−i}(K), so degrees 7 and 8 with ranks 2 and 1. Every original facet has 10 vertices (dimension9); nonzero lower-dimensional homology obstructs pure shellability. No statement about original Δ3 homotopy type or all Paley q.

value.rationale: An ordinary 3-cut complex is a canonical graph topological invariant, and Paley(13) is the smallest natural nontrivial quadratic-residue strongly regular graph with this local six-cycle link structure. Its mixed-dimensional Alexander-dual wedge and original pure non-shellability supply a finite exact structural example where general sphere-wedge criteria fail. The classification, torsion-freeness and shellability obstruction are useful for comparing ordinary and total cut constructions; this is not a gratuitous tiny arithmetic test.

final_claim: For P13 with residue edges and the ordinary three-cut complex Δ3(P13), its Alexander dual K has homotopy type S²∨S³∨S³, hence Δ3 has reduced integral H7=Z² and H8=Z, and the pure nine-dimensional cut complex is non-shellable.
limitations: Only the dual homotopy type, not the original cut-complex homotopy type, is identified.
Pure complex has homology below its pure top dimension; non-shellability follows via standard shellability theorem.
